name: Error message and stack formats
plain: Triggers errors and reads their message text and stack trace format.
meaning: Error wording and stack layout differ between V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore, and shift per version, revealing real engine under a spoofed user agent.

web.api: try { null.x } catch(e){ e.message, e.stack }; Error.captureStackTrace; Error.stackTraceLimit

steps: Compare message strings and stack frame syntax

limits.headline: Can trigger small errors to learn which browser engine you really use
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Cause harmless errors on purpose and look at the wording
Tell Chrome, Firefox and Safari engines apart by their error style
Guess the browser version from small changes in the wording
cannot: See anything you typed or saved
Know who you are by itself
Break the page or your device

story.what_it_is: A script causes small errors on purpose and reads the message and stack trace, which differ by browser.
story.for_you: You never see it. The page makes errors inside itself and reads the wording, which looks a little different in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. The result helps name your browser.
story.for_makers: Errors are a normal part of building apps, and sites collect them to fix bugs. Fraud tools also read the wording to tell real browsers from scripts that fake them.

use_cases.example: A website tracks crashes and sends error messages home to fix bugs.
A bot detector throws an error and sees a message style from an automation tool rather than a real browser.
A fingerprint library adds the error text format as one more clue in a device ID.
A browser game catches a missing feature error and shows a nicer message, or loads a simpler mode.
A web editor sends crash details to its team so a bug in one browser can be fixed fast.
An ad script checks the error format to spot that traffic comes from a headless browser.
A retailer logs checkout errors by browser to find which one breaks the payment form.

value.abuse: Detect UA spoofing and automation (for example missing stack frames)
